skill.name: ui-design
skill.description: A screenshot-first UI refinement workflow for layout, spacing, color, and component style changes. It uses ASCII diagrams, option selection, focused edits, and small follow-up adjustments.
skill.summary: Guide UI style changes with screenshots, ASCII layout options, focused edits, and targeted refinements.
skill.author: yunshu0909

security_audit.summary: Static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences around ASCII UI diagrams. The high-entropy heuristic is also a false positive because SKILL.md is readable Markdown with Chinese text, emoji, and box-drawing characters.

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.18 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 starts a Markdown code fence that contains an ASCII layout example, not executable Ruby or shell code. No command, interpreter call, or user-controlled execution path is present.
Line 31 closes the same Markdown code fence for the ASCII diagram. It is documentation syntax only and does not execute external commands.
Line 41 opens a Markdown code fence for alternative ASCII layout examples. The fenced content is visual documentation, not command execution.
The file is readable Markdown beginning with YAML front matter and Chinese prose. Higher entropy is explained by multilingual text, emoji, and box-drawing characters, not binary or encrypted content.

content.user_title: Guide UI Refinement with Screenshot Workflow
content.value_statement: UI changes often fail when layout issues are vague. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through screenshots, ASCII proposals, focused edits, and small refinements.
actual_capabilities: Requires reading the current implementation before suggesting visual changes.
Uses screenshots and marked areas to identify the exact UI problem.
Describes the current layout with ASCII diagrams for confirmation.
Presents two or three visual options before code changes begin.
Limits implementation to the selected UI change and supports direct micro-adjustments.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not a visual design engine.
It depends on user screenshots or clear visual descriptions.
It does not replace accessibility testing or browser QA.
It discourages broad refactors during small style changes.

use_cases.title: Refine dashboard spacing
use_cases.description: A frontend developer can align cards, controls, and headers after confirming the current layout.

use_cases.title: Compare layout alternatives
use_cases.description: A product designer can review two or three ASCII options before selecting a direction.

use_cases.title: Handle small visual feedback
use_cases.description: A product manager can request exact color, border, or spacing tweaks without reopening broad design choices.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the UI issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a screenshot or visual description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the attached UI screenshot. First read the related files, then describe the current layout with an ASCII diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Offer layout options
prompt_templates.scenario: The current layout is understood, but the target design is not chosen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show two or three layout options for the selected area. Include an ASCII diagram and one short reason for each option.

prompt_templates.title: Implement the selected option
prompt_templates.scenario: The user has chosen one design direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply option B only. Keep the edit focused on the selected layout change and avoid unrelated refactors.

prompt_templates.title: Refine after review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced follow-up after the first implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adjust only the spacing and border strength from the latest screenshot. Make the smallest change that addresses the feedback.

output_examples.input: The refresh button feels disconnected from the search box.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the current layout, then offers two ASCII alternatives that place search and refresh controls together or near the title.

output_examples.input: Option A is close, but the spacing is too tight.
output_examples.output: The assistant treats this as a micro-adjustment and changes only the spacing around the selected controls.

output_examples.input: Can you make this page feel cleaner?
output_examples.output: The assistant asks which area feels wrong and requests a screenshot before suggesting a broad redesign.

best_practices: Provide a screenshot with the target area clearly marked.
Confirm the current ASCII layout before selecting a design option.
Keep each implementation focused on one visual change.
anti_patterns: Starting code changes before the current UI is confirmed.
Offering only one layout option for a meaningful design choice.
Combining a small style request with unrelated refactoring.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps structure UI style changes for layout, spacing, color, and component arrangement.

faq.question: Does it generate final visual assets?
faq.answer: No. It guides design discussion and code edits, but it does not create standalone design files.

faq.question: Why does it ask for screenshots?
faq.answer: Screenshots reduce ambiguity and help the assistant identify the exact area that needs work.

faq.question: Can it handle quick tweaks?
faq.answer: Yes. After a design direction is chosen, small changes can be applied directly.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file is documentation only. Static command warnings were Markdown fence false positives.
